long_biography.plain_text:
American businessman Henry Luken established Telco Development Group, a computer-systems company, and Tel-Labs, a telephone-billing business, before co-founding Telco. A Kentucky native, he lived in Florida before his family moved to Chattanooga, where he would build several of his businesses.

His acquisition of Bob Corker's commercial-property portfolio brought office buildings and shopping premises under Luken Holdings. He retained the existing staff and management team, led by Kim White, while greatly enlarging his property business. He made some of his network hardware available for MetroNet, a nonprofit supplying Internet connectivity to businesses and residents in Chattanooga.
